I've fixed the reachable vulnerabilities by upgrading 11 production dependencies. Only `package.json` and `package-lock.json` changed; no source code needed to change. The backend tests pass (244/244, same as before), and the app works when driven end to end.

**What changed** (each version range kept to the project's required `~` style, which `extra/check-package-json.mjs` confirms):

| Package | Old → new | Why it's reachable |
|---|---|---|
| jsonata | 2.1.0 → 2.2.2 | Critical code-execution bugs. Users write JSONata expressions for HTTP/MQTT/MongoDB JSON-query monitors. |
| protobufjs | 7.2.6 → 7.6.6 | Critical code injection. The gRPC monitor parses `.proto` text supplied by the user. |
| @grpc/grpc-js | 1.8.22 → 1.14.7 | A malicious gRPC server can crash the client. |
| axios (+ follow-redirects 1.16.2) | 0.32.0 → 0.34.0 | Prototype-pollution and proxy-bypass bugs on all outgoing HTTP from monitors and notifications. |
| nodemailer | 7.0.13 → 10.3.1 | SMTP command/header injection, address-parser bugs and denial-of-service, in SMTP notifications and the SMTP monitor. |
| liquidjs | 10.26 → 10.30.1 | Template denial-of-service and memory-limit bypass in notification templates. |
| mysql2 | 3.11.5 → 3.24.6 | A malicious server can get the plaintext password or send a decompression bomb, via the MySQL monitor. |
| ws | 8.19.0 → 8.22.1 | Memory disclosure and denial-of-service in the WebSocket monitor. |
| qs | 6.14.2 → 6.17.1 | Denial-of-service bugs (qs is also used by express). |
| express 4.22.3, compression 1.8.2 (+ body-parser 1.20.9, proxy-addr 2.0.8, engine.io 6.6.11 pulled in through express and socket.io) | patch updates | Denial-of-service bugs and IP spoofing when `trustProxy` is turned on. |

For nodemailer 7 → 10, I checked the breaking changes and none apply here: the renamed error code isn't used, no remote attachments are fetched, and it needs Node ≥20, which the app already requires.

**Project policies:**
- **14-day release age (`.npmrc`):** npm 10.8.2 ignores `min-release-age`, so I installed with `--before=2026-11-01`. All 19 changed packages were published before that date. This means some of the versions `npm audit` suggested were off-limits (ws 8.23.0, nodemailer 10.5.0, axios 1.21.1, tar 7.5.23), so I picked older versions that still fix the issues.
- **Install-script allowlist:** protobufjs runs a postinstall script, so I changed its entry in `allowScripts` from `protobufjs@7.2.6` to `protobufjs@7.6.6`.

**How I checked it:**
- I started the server on a fresh SQLite database and drove it through socket.io against local fake servers: setup and login, then JSON-query, keyword, WebSocket, gRPC and SMTP monitors. All five came up healthy.
- An SMTP test notification with a Liquid template was delivered.
- The dashboard, gzip-compressed assets, status badges and the `/metrics` login check all still work.

The audit drops from 80 to 67 findings. Everything still flagged is either dev/build tooling or not reachable:
- **tar (critical):** only used by `extra/download-dist.js` to unpack the project's own release from a fixed GitHub HTTPS address, by release scripts, and by the sqlite3 build tools. Fixing it would mean a major upgrade plus script changes, and sqlite3 would still pull in the old tar anyway.
- **@azure/msal-node:** the SQL Server driver never uses the affected login flow.
- **undici:** the bundled copies are never used to make requests (cheerio only parses HTML here).
- **lodash, glob, minimatch:** used internally by the database libraries and never given user input.
- **ip-address:** its issues are server-side request forgery, which SECURITY.md says is out of scope.
- **gamedig / fast-xml-parser (low):** the only "fix" offered is a downgrade.
- **dompurify / vue-i18n / vite:** frontend build dependencies. The app doesn't use the affected DOMPurify modes or vue-i18n's `escapeParameter`, and it doesn't do server-side rendering.

`AGENTS.md` says the maintainers only accept AI-generated changes after a person has reviewed and tested them personally. If you plan to send this upstream, review and test it yourself first.
